What Each Major Component Does ### Client (React + Vite) | File | Purpose | |---|---| | **`vite.config.js`** | Configures Vite with the React plugin, Tailwind CSS v4, and Babel with the React Compiler preset for optimized React rendering. | | **`main.jsx`** | Entry point. Renders `` above all routes. | | **`BottomNav.jsx`** | A fixed bottom navigation bar built with MUI `BottomNavigation`. Four tabs: Chat, Dashboard, Camera, Settings. Each is a `` to its route. | | **`Chat.jsx`** | **The most substantial client component.** A full real-time chat client. On mount, it opens a WebSocket to `ws://localhost:3001`, stores a unique `clientId` in localStorage, receives chat history on connect, and sends/receives messages in real time. Displays messages as `ChatBubble` components. | | **`ChatBubble.jsx`** | A presentational component that renders a single chat message as a styled bubble (blue for own messages, white for others), with timestamp. | | **`ChatInput.jsx`** | A presentational textarea input with a send button (MUI IconButton + SendRoundedIcon). Handles Enter-to-send and shift+Enter for newlines. | | **`Placeholder.jsx`** | A minimal placeholder `

` for routes that are not yet implemented (home, camera, dashboard). | | **`Dashboard.jsx`** | Empty file -- reserved for a future admin dashboard component (imported but commented out in App.jsx). | | **`index.css`** | All CSS styling. Uses Tailwind `@apply` directives for a mobile-first chat UI: sticky header with online/offline pill, scrollable message list, sticky composer, styled bubbles, input box with focus ring, and send button. | **Key client dependencies:** - React 19, react-router-dom v7 - MUI v9 (`@mui/material`, `@mui/icons-material`, `@mui/x-chat`) - Dexie + PouchDB (IndexedDB wrappers -- imported in package.json but not yet used in code) - Tailwind CSS v4 ### Server (Node.js / Express) | File | Purpose | |---|---| | **`index.js`** | **Main server entry point.** Creates an Express app and an HTTP server on port 3001. Calls `attachChatServer(server)` to attach the WebSocket server to the same HTTP server, and `attachFaceServer(app)` to mount the facial recognition REST routes. Has a single `GET /` health-check endpoint. | | **`chatserver.cjs`** | **Real-time chat server.** Uses the `websocket` library (not socket.io, despite it being in package.json). Maintains a `Set` of connected clients. On connection, sends the full chat history from the database. On message, validates text (max 1000 chars) and senderId, persists to the database via `addmessage()`, then broadcasts to all connected clients. | | **`database/db.cjs`** | **Database connection and schema definition.** Connects to PostgreSQL via Sequelize using env vars (`DB_NAME`, `DB_USER`, `DB_PASSWORD`). Defines four models (see Database section below). Runs `sequelize.sync()` on import to ensure tables exist. | | **`database/dbcrudmethods.js`** | **ORM model classes** wrapping Sequelize models with a clean CRUD API. Exports `User` and `FaceEmbeddings` classes. `FaceEmbeddings.createFromImage()` is a higher-level method that calls the Python FaceNet server to extract face embeddings from an image, then stores each face in the database. | ### Facial Recognition Module (`modules/facial_recog/`) | File | Purpose | |---|---| | **`facialrecogserver.js`** | **Express REST API router** with three endpoints for face management. Mounted by `attachFaceServer(app)` in index.js. | | **`facenetClient.js`** | **Node.js client for the Python FaceNet server.** Manages the lifecycle of the Python subprocess (install pip deps, start uvicorn, wait for model load). Provides three async functions: `getFaceEmbedding()`, `detectFaces()`, and `getFaceEmbeddings()`. Communicates via HTTP POST to `http://127.0.0.1:8000`. | | **`startFaceNet.js`** | **Standalone launcher script** (run via `npm run dev` in server). Simply imports and calls `startPythonServer()`. | ### Python Server (`python_server/`) | File | Purpose | |---|---| | **`server.py`** | **FastAPI server** for AI inference. Loads the DeepFace Facenet model at startup. Exposes three endpoints (see below). Runs on `127.0.0.1:8000` via uvicorn. | | **`requirements.txt`** | Python dependencies: `fastapi`, `uvicorn`, `deepface`, `opencv-python`, `tf-keras`, `numpy`. | --- ## 3. How Client and Server Interact There are **two communication channels**: ### A. WebSocket Chat (real-time messaging) ``` Client (Chat.jsx) Server (chatserver.cjs) | | |--- WebSocket connect (ws://localhost:3001) --> | | |<-- { type: "history", messages: [...] } --| (full chat history from PostgreSQL) | | |--- { text, timestamp, senderId } ------->| (new message) | | |<-- { type: "message", message: {...} } --| (broadcast to ALL connected clients) ``` - The client opens a raw WebSocket connection (using the browser's native `WebSocket` API, NOT socket.io). - The server uses the `websocket` npm library to handle connections on the same HTTP server (port 3001). - Messages are persisted to PostgreSQL via `addmessage()` before broadcasting. - The client stores a `clientId` (UUID) in localStorage to distinguish its own messages from others. ### B. REST API (facial recognition) ``` Client (future camera UI) Server (facialrecogserver.js) | | |--- POST /api/user/:id/face ------------->| (register face: base64 image) | | -> calls Python /embed-all |<-- 201 [{ imageHash, embeddings }] ------| -> stores in PostgreSQL | | |--- PATCH /api/user/:id/face/default ---->| (set primary face) | | -> deletes old primary, creates new |<-- 200 [{ imageHash, embeddings }] ------| | | |--- GET /api/user/:id/face/default ------>| (get default face for user) |<-- 200 [{ imageHash, imageData, ... }] --| ``` The server-to-Python communication (Node to FastAPI): ``` Node (facenetClient.js) Python (server.py - FastAPI) | | |--- POST /embed (multipart form) -------->| DeepFace.represent() -> 128-d embedding |--- POST /detect (multipart form) ------->| DeepFace.extract_faces() -> bounding boxes |--- POST /embed-all (multipart form) ---->| Both: detect + embed each face ``` The Node server manages the Python process as a child process. It: 1. Installs pip dependencies from `requirements.txt` if needed 2. Spawns `python server.py` 3. Waits for the stdout message "Facenet model loaded successfully" before accepting requests --- ## 4. Database **PostgreSQL** via **Sequelize** ORM (v6). Connection is configured in `db.cjs` using environment variables: - `DB_NAME`, `DB_USER`, `DB_PASSWORD` (from `.env` at project root) - Host: `localhost`, Dialect: `postgres` ### Tables / Models | Model | Table Name | Fields | Purpose | |---|---|---|---| | **User** | `users` | `id` (UUID PK, auto-generated), `enName` (STRING, required), `zhName` (STRING, nullable) | Registered users. Supports English and Chinese names. | | **Messages** | `messages` | `content` (STRING), `timestamp` (DATE), `senderId` (UUID FK -> users.id) | Chat messages. Has a belongsTo relationship with User. | | **FaceEmbeddings** | `faceEmbeddings` | `imageHash` (STRING PK, SHA-256 of face image), `userId` (UUID FK -> users.id), `imageType` (STRING: "primary" or "cache"), `imageData` (BLOB), `embeddings` (STRING, JSON), `model` (STRING) | Stores face images and their 128-dimensional Facenet embeddings. "primary" = user's default face for recognition; "cache" = additional uploaded faces. | | **Attendee** | `attendees` | `name` (STRING) | Placeholder model for event attendees (not yet used in routes). | | **Admin** | `admins` | `name` (STRING), `privileges` (STRING) | Placeholder model for admin users (not yet used in routes). | Relationships: `messages.belongsTo(user)` and `user.hasMany(messages)` via `senderId`. Schema is synced on server startup via `sequelize.sync({ force: false })` (creates tables if they don't exist, does not drop). --- ## 5. AI / Facial Recognition Features ### Architecture The AI system is a **three-tier architecture**: Client -> Node.js (orchestration) -> Python (inference). ### AI Model - **DeepFace** library with the **Facenet** model (Google's FaceNet, producing 128-dimensional embeddings per face). - The model is loaded once at Python server startup and reused for all requests. ### Endpoints (Python FastAPI, port 8000) | Endpoint | Method | Input | Output | What it does | |---|---|---|---|---| | `/embed` | POST | Image file (multipart) | `{ success, embedding: number[128] }` | Generates a 128-d embedding for the single face in the image. | | `/detect` | POST | Image file (multipart) | `{ success, faces: [{x,y,w,h}] }` | Detects all faces and returns bounding box coordinates. | | `/embed-all` | POST | Image file (multipart) | `{ success, faces: [{ faceImage(base64), embedding, bbox }] }` | Detects all faces, crops each one, generates embeddings, and returns the cropped face images (base64) along with embeddings and bounding boxes. | ### REST API (Express, port 3001) | Endpoint | Method | Purpose | |---|---|---| | `POST /api/user/:id/face` | POST | **Register a face.** Accepts a base64 image, calls Python to detect and embed all faces, stores each as a "cache" type FaceEmbedding in the database. | | `PATCH /api/user/:id/face/default` | PATCH | **Set primary face.** Deletes existing primary face(s) for the user, then processes the new image and stores it as "primary" type. | | `GET /api/user/:id/face/default` | GET | **Retrieve primary face.** Returns the image data (base64), embeddings, and model info for the user's default face. | ### Client-side Libraries (installed but not yet wired up) - `dexie` + `dexie-react-hooks` (IndexedDB wrapper) - `pouchdb` (local database) - `react-native-sqlite-storage` (SQLite -- likely for future offline/local face caching) ### Python Dependencies - `deepface` -- The core AI library - `tf-keras` -- TensorFlow/Keras backend for DeepFace - `opencv-python` (cv2) -- Image loading, cropping, encoding - `numpy` -- Array operations - `fastapi` + `uvicorn` -- HTTP server framework --- ## Summary of Project State **OpenGlimpse** is an AI-powered web application for quick registration and verification at events using facial recognition. The project has: - **Working:** Real-time WebSocket chat (client + server + database persistence) - **Working:** Facial recognition pipeline (Python inference via DeepFace/Facenet, Node orchestration, PostgreSQL storage for embeddings) - **Working:** User and face management REST API - **Stubbed/Placeholder:** Camera page, Dashboard page, Settings/Home page (all currently render placeholder text) - **Unused but installed:** Dexie/PouchDB for local client-side storage; socket.io (server has the `websocket` library instead) The chat feature is fully functional end-to-end. The facial recognition backend is fully implemented (detection, embedding generation, storage, retrieval), but the client-side camera UI that would drive it has not been built yet -- it is currently a Placeholder component at the `/camera` route.
